name: Muhlenbergia

flags: muhlenbergia-piniflora — provisional source-concept learner; the source name appears erroneous and the species package must remain visibly flagged until provenance is corrected.

muhlenbergia-paniculata — Kew accepts the NAME (Muhlenbergia paniculata, synonym Schedonnardus paniculatus); existing source PHOTO species determination, fine unilateral spikelet rows and local range were not independently re-reviewed. Not a finalized visual anchor.
project_scope.note: Seven installed canonical concepts counted; M. piniflora source-concept ID and M. paniculata taxonomy/photo reviews remain flagged, not accepted as genus-key finished.

recognition.where_to_look_first: The project set spans large fountain-form bunchgrasses, small tight bunchgrasses, creeping nimblewill, and rhizomatous low muhly. Start with growth form and scale, then inspect the ligule, leaf folding/rolling, and panicle size and openness.
priority: upright bunchgrass versus creeping/rooting or rhizomatous habit
flat versus folded or involute blades
open feathery versus narrow contracted panicle
spikelet size and awn detail when the habit split is not enough

quick_split: M. lindheimeri — a LARGE coarse dense fountain clump with tall relatively contracted flower panicles and long membranous ligules.
M. reverchonii — SMALLER, more finely textured erect tuft with an airy, delicate panicle; compare true ligule and spikelet with lindheimeri.
M. schreberi — LOW weak creeping stems with short sideways leaves and narrow nearly spike-like panicle; may root from stolon nodes.
M. utilis — LOW rhizomatous grass with hair-fine inward-rolled leaves, SCALY underground rhizomes and small narrow often partly enclosed panicle.
M. paniculata (tumblegrass; formerly Schedonnardus paniculatus) — a few very LONG, slender, widely diverging one-sided racemes, often curving; look at branch shape instead of cloudlike plumes.
M. ×involuta — natural HYBRID of lindheimeri × reverchonii; intermediate stature/folded blades, but NEVER identify solely by parent-like habit.
M. piniflora — SOURCE NAME UNRESOLVED; not a taxonomically reliable field diagnosis or finished card.
comparison_lesson.nursery_warning: Do not use pink plume color by itself to call a plant M. lindheimeri. The widely sold M. capillaris concept is not a project-native Central Texas anchor.

visual_needs: Matched close-up membranous LIGULE for M. lindheimeri vs M. reverchonii.
Actual aboveground stolon NODE ISSUING ROOTS for M. schreberi, plus a separate tiny ligule and contracted mature panicle.
Genuinely exposed underground SCALY RHIZOME, rolled leaf cross-section, and small mature inflorescence for M. utilis.
Paniculata: clear TWO ROWS of spikelets on ONE SIDE of slender divergent raceme; full plant and twisted leaves.
An exact taxon-correct, reuse-permitted, verified live M. ×involuta PHOTO; existing multigrass historic plate/parent pictures do not fill this gap.
Resolve the original source concept / scientific identity of M. piniflora before visual species-ID training.
Species-level lookalike closeup of M. lindheimeri, M. reverchonii and natural hybrid ×involuta on matched scale.
visual_status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: five source-photographed species with conservative comparisons; M. ×involuta lacks an exact validated live image; M. piniflora remains taxonomic source HOLD; tumblegrass source photo ID remains unreviewed.

fast_fill_note: Current learner coverage: M. schreberi 3 images; M. lindheimeri 2; M. reverchonii 1; M. utilis 1; M. ×involuta 1. M. piniflora remains excluded from fast-fill because its canonical record is scientifically PROVISIONAL and likely represents an erroneous source name. Do not pad wild-type lessons with named cultivars or uncertain-rights media.
look_here_first: Start at the WHOLE plant: large dense upright fountain and contracted dense flowering head (M. lindheimeri); small tightly tufted fine-leaved plant (M. reverchonii); short SIDEWAYS-leaved jointed low stems (M. schreberi); exceptionally fine LOW patch that must be checked for SCALY rhizomes (M. utilis); or few LONG widely diverging racemes (M. paniculata). Next find true collar/ligule, rooting node OR underground rhizome where relevant, and mature spikelet. These are DIFFERENT pathways, not proof from one photo. Hybrid ×involuta needs true exact-hybrid evidence; piniflora remains a non-identifiable source hold.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHOLE PLANT FIRST: upright tuft, above-ground runner, below-ground rhizome, or long spreading racemes. THEN collar and spikelets.

comparison_matrix.caution: UT Austin local seep muhly ligule length and broad GrassBase ranges differ; do not force absolute mm cutoffs. Growth size alone is supporting. M. capillaris is a nursery look-alike, not a project-local native anchor.
